answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity. Every agent that wants into a task pool locks a deposit, and random peers grade its work. If an answer is judged fraudulent, part of the deposit gets slashed. A sybil attacker needs a separate locked deposit for each fake identity, so a thousand fake agents means a thousand stakes at risk. Reputation builds slowly, like karst forming over years, so new identities earn little trust. Audit results go to a ferrous-hard, append-only ledger, so one bad ripple of fake work cannot be quietly erased.
